PDF data extraction for spreadsheet entr: Use openpyxl/pandas to read the result xlsx and compare specific cell values (numeric) with approx tolerance via check_cell rules; the compare_table metric supports 'approx:N' method for floating-point amounts extracted from PDFs.

When verifying transaction amounts parsed from PDF receipts/invoices, use sheet_fuzzy exact_match for text fields (category, description) and check_cell approx match for numeric fields (amounts, running balances).

Running balance/cumulative columns can be verified by checking each row's cell value independently with approx tolerance rather than comparing full column ranges, since small extraction errors compound.

PDF text extraction tools (pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, pdfminer) vary in how they parse tables vs. free-form text; verify that currency symbols, negative signs, and decimal separators are correctly parsed before numeric comparison.
Use fitz (PyMuPDF) to extract text from each page via page.get_text() and compare with fuzz.ratio for fuzzy text similarity scoring
PDF file organization/copying into folde: Verify the correct PDF ends up at the target path by extracting and fuzzy-comparing its text content against a reference PDF; fitz.open + page.get_text() is the standard extraction approach, and fuzz.ratio >= threshold indicates a match
PDF form filling from spreadsheet data: Use PyMuPDF (fitz) to extract text from each page and compare against reference PDFs using fuzzy string matching (e.g., fuzz.ratio) averaged across multiple files.
When verifying checkbox/mark fields, extract raw text and check for presence of the specific mark character (e.g., √) in the correct positions relative to surrounding label text.
For multi-file batch output, iterate over all expected output files and average similarity scores; a missing file should contribute 0 to the score.
PDF text extraction via fitz page.get_text() captures both static text and filled form field values as a flat string, making fuzz.ratio a practical similarity metric for form content comparison.
PDF file naming based on data field valu: Check that output filenames exactly match the employee/entity name strings as they appear in the source data, including spaces and capitalization.
Use os.path.exists or directory listing to verify each expected filename is present before attempting content comparison.
PDF author identification: Author order (first, last N) must be extracted from PDF metadata or rendered text; use PDF parsing libraries to read author lists from title pages or headers.

Verification relies on cross-referencing extracted author names against expected personal webpage URLs, so the checker must tolerate multiple valid URL aliases per author (use itertools.product over per-author URL sets and compare as sets).
Image to PDF conversion: Use fitz (PyMuPDF) to extract embedded images from each PDF page via page.get_images() and pdf_document.extract_image(); compare extracted images between result and reference using perceptual hashing (e.g., imagehash.phash) with a small hash-difference threshold to tolerate minor encoding differences
Check that the number of embedded images across all pages matches between result and reference PDF before doing content comparison
When a PDF is created by embedding an image, the image may be re-encoded (JPEG, PNG, etc.); perceptual hash comparison is more robust than pixel-exact or byte-exact comparison for this feature class
